findings.evidence: The skill directory tracks only SKILL.md and codemod_template.py.txt. It has no evals/evals.json and no evals/trigger-queries.json. It ships no runnable code (the template is .txt), so the 8/7 split applies. tests/test_gate_scope.py, tests/test_setup.py and tests/test_wizard_app_1.py only check paths and titles, not codemod behaviour.
findings.fix: Add evals/evals.json with 3 or more prompts. Include a casual multi-file class rename, a parameter rename across call sites, and an edge case where the name collides with a stdlib attribute such as `connect` or `run`. Put sample .py inputs in evals/files/. Use verifiable assertions, such as 'comments and strings that contain the old name are unchanged' and 'sqlite3.connect is untouched or flagged'. Add evals/trigger-queries.json with about 20 queries, 8-10 positive and 8-10 near-miss negatives, such as a one-line rename, a JS rename, or a ruff autofix.

findings.evidence: "LibCST parses source into a Concrete Syntax Tree, matches syntax nodes (not raw text), transforms them, and serializes back". Notes also say "Validate changes with tests after codemod runs." and "Prefer `uv run python` unless your venv is already active."
findings.fix: Delete the Overview paragraph and the generic Notes bullets (validate with tests, run from project root, prefer uv run, and the line that repeats the string/comment rule). Keep only the note that codemods touch only .py files.

findings.evidence: Preconditions and Examples are listed, but no ordered workflow runs from the clean tree through a pilot run, diff audit and widening --paths to the tests and a grep for leftover dynamic references.
findings.fix: Add a short numbered procedure. 1) Check for a clean tree. 2) Grep the old name to list dynamic, string and config hits. 3) Run on one module. 4) Review `git diff`, including collateral matches on other libraries' attributes. 5) Widen --paths. 6) Run the tests. 7) Grep the old name again and fix the remaining dynamic references by hand.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list is strong, but no Gotchas cover the template's own surprises. For example, `--include-tests` appends `tests` even when it is not a directory, and `rename-symbol` also renames import aliases and keyword arguments with the same name.
findings.fix: Add a Gotchas section of 2-4 verified template behaviours: what happens to `from x import Old` and to `Old` as a keyword argument name, and what happens when tests/ is missing with --include-tests.

findings.evidence: The description has WHAT and WHEN but no 'not for' boundary against near misses (single-line edits, non-Python code, lint autofixes). It also does not say that it applies even when the user never names LibCST.
findings.fix: Use when renaming or changing signatures across many Python files where comments, formatting and string contents must survive: rename a class, method, constant or function parameter, add or remove a parameter and update call sites, or rewrite a scoped docstring. Applies even when the user never mentions LibCST or codemods and just asks to 'rename X everywhere' in a Python repo. Bundles codemod_template.py.txt (copy to tools/codemod_template.py) with the subcommands rename-symbol, rename-parameter, add-parameter, remove-parameter and rewrite-docstring. Matching is by name only, with no scope or type resolution. Not for single-line or single-file edits, non-Python code, or lint and format autofixes.

findings.evidence: Bootstrapping always describes copying the 478-line template. Nothing says not to read the template file into context, and nothing points the agent to the template's `--help` to learn its interface.
findings.fix: Add: 'Do not read codemod_template.py.txt into context; copy it, then run `uv run python tools/codemod_template.py <subcommand> --help` for flags. Read it only when writing a custom transformer (for example one using QualifiedNameProvider).'

findings.evidence: "Use the `context7:query-docs` skill (or `mcp__context7__query-docs`) to confirm LibCST APIs when needed." and line 28 "`uv add --dev \"libcst>=1.5,<2\"` or whatever the project lock requires"
findings.fix: Give one default: read the version in the project's lockfile, and use the uv command only when LibCST is missing. Make context7 conditional ('only when you write a custom transformer'), with a fallback when it is not installed.

findings.evidence: "There is no `--dry-run` flag: run on one file or module first, inspect `git diff`, then expand `--paths`." The skill has no validation loop with an exit criterion, does not say how to recognise and fix a parse failure on a file, and gives no rollback command for a bad partial run.
findings.fix: Add a validation loop: after each run, review `git diff --stat` and the full diff, and run the tests. If unrelated matches appear, run `git restore <paths>` and narrow --paths or switch to a QualifiedNameProvider codemod. Repeat until the diff contains only intended changes and the tests pass. Also state what the script does when a file fails to parse.
